context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Stop returning the whole `updatedUser` model. Build the response from an explicit allow-list of fields that the requester is entitled to see, for example `const { id, name, email, updatedAt } = updatedUser;` then `res.json({ id, name, email, updatedAt });`. Exclude sensitive or unneeded fields such as password hashes, tokens, internal flags, and nested records. Put the allow-list in one shared serializer (e.g., `toPublicUser(user, requester)`) and use it on every route that returns this user record, so the same field limits apply everywhere, as the guidance requires. Add a test that asserts the response contains only the allowed keys and none of the excluded ones.
